title: Conormal and strict-transform geometry for a regular flag
statement:
Let $Z\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{j}X$ be regular closed immersions of Noetherian schemes of constant codimensions $m,n>0$. Regular means locally cut out by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Write $N_{X/Y}=I_Y/I_Y^2$ for the conormal module, and similarly for other immersions. For every regular closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow V$ of Noetherian schemes of constant codimension $c\geq0$ (a single one, not necessarily part of a flag), its conormal module is finite locally free of rank $c$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]; in particular the conormal modules of $i$, $j$ and $ji$ are finite locally free of ranks $m$, $n$ and $m+n$. Their natural sequence is exact:
$$0\to i^*N_{X/Y}\to N_{X/Z}\to N_{Y/Z}\to0.$$
Write $\operatorname{Bl}_W V=\operatorname{Proj}_V\bigoplus_{a\geq0}I_W^a$ and $P(F)=\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{Sym}F)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_Y X\to X$, the exceptional subscheme is $P=P(N_{X/Y})$, an effective Cartier divisor, with $\mathcal I_P=\mathcal O_B(1)$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Put $P'=P\times_Y Z$ and let $p:P\to Y$, $p':P'\to Z$, $i':P'\hookrightarrow P$, $j':P\hookrightarrow B$. Then $i'$ has codimension $m$ and $j'i'$ codimension $m+1$. The natural conormal maps give surjections
$$p^*N_{X/Y}\twoheadrightarrow N_{B/P},\qquad p'^*N_{X/Z}\twoheadrightarrow N_{B/P'}.$$
Their kernels $K$ and $K'$ are vector bundles of rank $n-1$, with the canonical isomorphism $i'^*K\cong K'$. The conormal of $i'$ identifies with $p'^*N_{Y/Z}$.
If $n=1$, instead take $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X$, let $P=P(N_{X/Z})$ be its exceptional divisor, and let $\widetilde Y=\operatorname{Bl}_Z Y$ be the strict transform of $Y$. Then $\widetilde Y\hookrightarrow B$ is an effective Cartier divisor, $P'=P(N_{Y/Z})=P\cap\widetilde Y$, and $P$ and $\widetilde Y$ meet transversely (their intersection is an effective Cartier divisor on each). If $I=\mathcal I_Y$, then
$$\pi^*I\cong\mathcal I_P\otimes\mathcal I_{\widetilde Y}$$
as invertible modules with their canonical trivializations off $\pi^{-1}Y$. Put $K_0=i^*N_{X/Y}$, a line on $Z$. The ideal of $P'\subset P$ is $p_P^*K_0\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$, where $p_P:P\to Z$ is the projective bundle projection. No regularity of the ambient schemes is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, pp. 234-235 (conormal diagram and its kernels), and proof of Theorem 2.3.2, pp. 236-237 (strict-transform factorization and hyperplane ideal).

proof.text: Work locally at a point of the relevant center. For this purpose localization commutes with the displayed constructions: $(S^{-1}I)^a=S^{-1}(I^a)$, so it commutes with the Rees algebra and all its degree-zero homogeneous charts; it also commutes with the ideal quotients presenting conormals. Thus calculations over the Noetherian local ring $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ test the desired sheaf maps and regularity at points above $x$. Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ for $I_Y$ and lifts $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ of regular generators for $I_{Z/Y}$. The concatenation $(f,g)$ is regular by the successive-nonzerodivisor definition. The permutation lemma applies with the finite module $M=R$; consequently any chosen $f_a$ or $g_b$ can be placed first, and any prefix of the $g$'s can be placed before all the $f$'s. Outside the center a center generator is a unit and its blowup chart is just the original open.

source.place: XVI 2.3.3, local regular equations for the diagram; algebra.tex Tag 00LJ, lemma-permute-xi, and Tag 00LF, definition-regular-sequence.

proof.text: For a single regular immersion of codimension $c$, the affine conormal identification and regular-sequence basis theorem give $I/I^2$ free on the $c$ equations. These local identifications prove finite local freeness of rank $c$; for $c=0$ the ideal and conormal are zero on a neighborhood of the source. Apply this also to $f$, $\bar g$ and $(f,g)$. Over $R/J$, $J=(f,g)$, the natural conormal sequence is the inclusion of the first $n$ basis vectors followed by projection onto the last $m$ basis vectors. It is therefore short exact, with the stated ranks. This proves the composite is regular as well, without requiring $R$ to be a regular local ring.

source.place: XVI 2.3.1 and 2.3.3, conormal bundles and the middle row of the diagram; Stacks Tags 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal) and 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), degree one.

proof.text: For any of these positive-codimension centers $I=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, use the finite covering by charts $C_a=R[I/h_a]$. The chart presentation is $C_a=R[u_i:i\ne a]/(h_a u_i-h_i)$. By the definition of the chart as a subalgebra of $R_{h_a}$, multiplication by $h_a$ is injective. The extended center ideal is $(h_a)$, and $C_a/(h_a)=(R/I)[u_i:i\ne a]$. Hence its inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor. The canonical graded map $\operatorname{Sym}_{R/I}(I/I^2)\to\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is an isomorphism by the regular-sequence graded-polynomial theorem (on the basis $[h_i]$ it sends each monomial to its actual ideal-power class). Equivalently the displayed divisor charts glue as $P(I/I^2)$. On overlaps the ideal generators satisfy $h_a=(h_a/h_b)h_b$, precisely the degree-one twist transition; this identifies its ideal with $\mathcal O_B(1)$. All identifications use the canonical homogeneous fractions, so respect localization and changes of equations.

source.place: XVI 2.3.3, identification of P and its Cartier immersion; Stacks Tags 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence) and 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular).

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to the blowup of $Y$. On its $f_a$-chart $C_a$, $P$ has equation $f_a$, and $P'$ has ideal $(f_a,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. Modulo $f_a$ the chart ring is $(R/I_Y)[u_i]$. The sequence $\bar g$ remains regular there: multiplication is coefficientwise injective after each prefix quotient. Thus $i'$ is regular of codimension $m$ and $j'i'$ is regular of codimension $m+1$. The conormal basis of $i'$ is the classes of $g_b$, so the natural map $p'^*N_{Y/Z}\to N_{P/P'}$ is an isomorphism. The projective-bundle base-change identification gives $P'=P(N_{X/Y}|_Z)$ and agrees with these charts; no assertion of stability under arbitrary nonflat base change is needed.

source.place: XVI 2.3.3, cartesian diagram and codimensions of i prime and j prime i prime; Stacks 00LN, 01R3, and constructions.tex Tag 01O3, lemma-relative-proj-base-change.

proof.text: In the $f_a$-chart put $u_a=1$. The natural map $p^*N_{X/Y}\to N_{B/P}$ sends $[f_i]$ to $u_i[f_a]$. It is surjective, and its kernel has basis $e_i-u_i e_a$ for $i\ne a$: the coefficient of $e_a$ is forced by the single equation $\sum_i u_i v_i=0$. On $P'$ the natural map $p'^*N_{X/Z}\to N_{B/P'}$ sends $[f_i]$ to $u_i[f_a]$ and $[g_b]$ to $[g_b]$. The target has the free basis $[f_a],[g_1],\ldots,[g_m]$ by Step 4. Its kernel therefore has exactly the same $n-1$ basis vectors, with all $g$ coordinates zero. These formulas prove both surjections and the ranks. Inclusion of the first summand in the canonical conormal sequence maps $i'^*K$ into $K'$ and is an isomorphism on these bases. Since it is induced by the canonical ideal maps, the local isomorphisms agree on overlaps. For $n=1$ both kernels are zero.

source.place: XVI 2.3.3, printed p.235, exact conormal diagram and canonical isomorphism of its kernels.

proof.text:
Now assume $n=1$ and write $f=f_1$, $J=(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. Apply Step 3 to $J$ to obtain the exceptional divisor $P=P(N_{X/Z})$ on $B=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X$. On the $g_b$-chart set $a=g_b$ and write
$$C=R[t,u_l:l\ne b]/(at-f,au_l-g_l),\qquad t=f/a.$$
This is the regular-sequence chart presentation after the permitted permutation in Step 1. Setting $t=0$ yields precisely $(R/(f))[(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_m)/\bar g_b]$, again by that chart presentation, now for the regular sequence $\bar g$ in $R/(f)$. In particular $a$ is a nonzerodivisor on $C/(t)$, since this latter ring is a subalgebra of $(R/(f))_a$. Also $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $C\subset R_a$, since it is one on $R$. As $f=at$, $t$ is a nonzerodivisor on $C$.

source.place: XVI 2.3.2, printed p.236, blowup along Z and its strict transform; Stacks 0BIQ, lemma-blowup-regular-sequence, applied in R and R/(f).

proof.text:
On this chart $Y\times_X B$ has ideal $(f)=(at)$, and its open away from the exceptional divisor is obtained by inverting $a$. Its scheme-theoretic closure has ideal
$$\ker(C\to(C/(at))_a)=(t):a^\infty=(t),$$
the last equality following from injectivity of $a$ on $C/(t)$. On the $f$-chart the analogous closure is empty, since $(C/(f))_f=0$. These are exactly the charts of $\operatorname{Bl}_Z Y$: the $g_b$-chart rings were identified in Step 6 and their transition maps send each ratio $\bar g_l/\bar g_b$ to the same ratio. They therefore glue to the claimed strict transform $\widetilde Y$, whose immersion is effective Cartier because its local equation $t$ is a nonzerodivisor (and is the unit equation on the $f$-chart).

source.place: XVI 2.3.2, printed p.236, strict-transform diagram; Stacks divisors.tex, lemma-strict-transform (Tag 080E), affine proof by removing exceptional-power torsion.

proof.text:
On a $g_b$-chart $P$ is $a=0$, $\widetilde Y$ is $t=0$, and
$$C/(a)=(R/J)[t,u_l:l\ne b],\qquad C/(a,t)=(R/J)[u_l:l\ne b].$$
Thus $t$ is a nonzerodivisor on $P$, while $a$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\widetilde Y$ by Step 6. This proves transverse Cartier intersection in both orders. Its charts are precisely those of $P(N_{Y/Z})$, and their ratio transition maps are those of this projective bundle; the intersection has no part in the $f$-chart. The product of the two divisor ideals is $(a)(t)=(f)$ on every $g_b$-chart and $(f)(1)=(f)$ on the $f$-chart. Multiplication therefore gives the asserted global isomorphism $\mathcal I_P\otimes\mathcal I_{\widetilde Y}\simeq\pi^*I$. It agrees with the canonical embeddings into $\mathcal O_B$, so on the complement of $\pi^{-1}Y$ it sends $1\otimes1$ to $1$ and preserves the specified trivializations.

source.place: XVI 2.3.2, printed p.236, transverse intersection and canonical ideal factorization.

proof.text: Finally write $F=N_{X/Z}$, $E=N_{Y/Z}$ and $K_0=i^*N_{X/Y}$. Step 2 gives the canonical exact sequence $0\to K_0\to F\to E\to0$, with $K_0$ a line. It locally splits simply by lifting a basis of the free quotient $E$; the lifts together with a basis of $K_0$ form a basis of $F$. On $P(F)$ compose $p_P^*K_0\to p_P^*F$ with the tautological quotient to $\mathcal O_P(1)$. In these bases its zero subscheme is exactly $P(E)$: its equation in a $g_b$-chart is $T_f/T_{g_b}=t$, and in the $f$-chart it is a unit. Twisting this map by $\mathcal O_P(-1)$ gives an injective map $p_P^*K_0\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)\to\mathcal O_P$ with image the ideal of $P'$. Injectivity is the polynomial nonzerodivisor calculation in Step 8. As the map was defined by the canonical inclusion and quotient, these identifications glue independently of the splitting. This proves the stated sign of the twist without identifying conormal bundles with their duals.

source.place: XVI 2.3.2, printed p.237, hyperplane ideal K tensor O(-1); Stacks constructions.tex, Tags 01OA and 01OB, projective-bundle quotient convention.
